prompts: We playtested two versions of the Pixel Arena tutorial and have to pick one for the next release. The export and its notes are in {WS}/telemetry. Should we ship B instead of A? Give a recommendation a skeptical lead would accept. Record it in {WS}/result.json with ship_b, sessions_a, sessions_b, completion_rate_a, completion_rate_b and p_value.
answers:
[goal] Decide whether tutorial variant B beats A under the 5% release rule, and record it in ./result.json.

[action] Read `telemetry/README.md` (export quirks + release rule), cleaned `telemetry/playtest_ab.csv` in `analyze_playtest.py`: deduped on `session_id` (1870 rows → 1800 unique sessions, 70 byte-identical resends, 0 conflicts), normalised `variant` (`' A'`, `'a'`, `'A'` → `a`). Then four tests, because 366 of 763 players appear in both arms so sessions are not independent: player-cluster bootstrap (20k draws), two-proportion z, Fisher exact, and a within-player paired test on the 366 crossover players. Also checked assignment balance over session-id blocks (no time drift: 150/150 per block) and match_minutes as context.

[result] Ship B. 900 sessions per arm, completion 38.00% (A) vs 46.67% (B), +8.67 pp, 95% CI +3.85 to +13.30 pp.

| test | unit | p |
|---|---|---|
| player-cluster bootstrap (reported `p_value`) | player | 0.0006 |
| two-proportion z (z=3.72) | session | 0.0002 |
| Fisher exact | session | 0.00024 |
| within-player paired (n=366, +9.04 pp) | player | 0.0052 |

All four clear 5%. The paired test is the load-bearing one: it compares the same players across arms, so the effect cannot be player-composition luck. Caveat stated in the JSON: restricting to players who saw only one arm gives +6.7 pp but p=0.09 at n=634, i.e. underpowered, not contradictory. Assumptions: `session_id` is the analysis unit, `completed_tutorial` is the ship metric, `match_minutes` is context only, reported p is the conservative clustered one.

Files: `analyze_playtest.py` (regenerates everything), `result.json` (`ship_b=true`, `sessions_a=900`, `sessions_b=900`, `completion_rate_a=0.38`, `completion_rate_b=0.4667`, `p_value=0.0006`, plus effect/tests/data-quality/assumptions blocks).

[next] Nothing needed for the release decision. If you want the crossover players explained (why 48% of players saw both arms in an A/B), that is an instrumentation question for arena-panel, not a stats one.

How I know it is right: every number above is printed by `python analyze_playtest.py`, which reads only the export and recomputes from raw rows; no browser or external tool was opened, so nothing to close.
